jamie: heads-up: canary on ded10 started hitting intermittent OOMs during long-chat load tests. I traced it to the prefetch path — it launches a shadow kernel, allocs a scratchpad, then returns. looks like it fragments the logits slab.

arjun: any profiler output? allocation counts / sizes / which allocator? slab vs pool?

jamie: pasted a short profiler snapshot below (from the canary run):
```
--- profiler summary ---
cudaMalloc calls: 24
peak GPU mem: 14.7GB
largest transient allocs:
 - 4.2MB (logits temp) x3
 - 12.8MB (scratchpad prefetch) x1
allocator fragmentation: 18%
KV cache active per-request: 18MB
sequence len distribution: 16% >1024
```

leah: interesting — the prefetch kernel variant we're picking uses a different workspace alignment (4B) and forces slab splits. if we force the prefetch to reuse the existing logits slab or request a page-aligned scratchpad (64B), we should avoid creating small fragments.

arjun: quick experiment idea: change kernel-selection heuristic to prefer variants with identical workspace footprint as the active/serve path ("kernel congruence"). fallback to prefetch-only for seq < 256. also add a prefetch handshake: before allocating the prefetch scratchpad, try an N+1 reclaim on the logits pool. if reclaim fails, abort prefetch and run the cold kernel.

jamie: I ran a tiny patch that reuses the logits slab for prefetch; canary passed 1k requests with zero OOMs. PR #4123 has the diff. core bit: 
```
if (kernel.variant.fwsize == active_fwsize) {
  use_shared_slab(logits_slab);
} else {
  allocate_prefetch_scratch();
}
```

sara: telemetry shows a ~26% reduction in peak transient allocs in that canary. still seeing rare thrash at very high concurrency (~80 concurrent clients).

jamie: for high concurrency i think we need cooperative eviction: prefetch emits an async hint to KV cache to evict least-recent prefixes. if eviction can't free enough contiguous space, abort prefetch and avoid the alloc. cheaper to run the cold kernel than to risk OOM.

arjun: yep. also instrument metrics: prefetch_aborts, prefetch_evictions, kernel_switch_count. use those to gate enabling prefetch in production (A/B).

infra-bot: deploy-canary triggered for eng-runtime/dedicated/canary-3 by jamie at 2026-03-15T09:12Z :rocket:

leah: nice. i'll add a small defensive rule in the allocator: don't split a slab if the resulting fragment would be <2MB — keep fragments available for logits reuse. sending a review shortly.

jamie: @leah great, i'll add a unit test that simulates KV-heavy high-seq loads. thanks all :thumbsup:
